h1: The 8 Best Air Fryers Under $100 in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Air Fryers Under $100 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 air fryers under $100, scored on basket size, fan power, temperature range, coating, dual-zone cooking and ease of cleaning.
summary: The Cosori TurboBlaze 6-quart is the best air fryer under $100, with a fast fan, 90 to 450F temperature control, a PFAS-free ceramic basket and a quiet motor. The OLIXIS dual-basket model is the best for cooking two foods at once, the Ninja AF141 is the best 5-quart from a trusted brand, and the bella slim is the best compact model.
intro: Quarts are the number everyone looks at, and they are the least useful measure of an air fryer. A basket that is deep and narrow holds food in a thick pile that cooks unevenly, while a wide, shallow one spreads food out and crisps it. Under $100 the smarter buys are the shapes that give you surface area, plus a fan strong enough to move air through the pile.

That is how we ranked these eight, looking at basket shape and capacity, fan and wattage specifications, temperature range, coating material and extras like dual zones or a window. We reviewed listings and specs rather than cooking with each fryer. Where the maker quotes an oil-saving or fat-reduction figure we leave it out, because those numbers depend on the test, and several models are in the $50 to $100 range, near the top of this budget.

products.name: Cosori TurboBlaze Air Fryer, 9-in-1, 6 Qt, PFAS-Free Ceramic Coating
products.verdict: A 3600 rpm fan, five fan speeds and a PFAS-free ceramic basket under 53 dB.
products.description:
The TurboBlaze has a 6-quart square basket, a 3600 rpm fan with five speeds, and temperature control from 90 to 450F. The basket and crisper tray use a PFAS-free ceramic coating, and the listing puts the noise level below 53 dB even at the top fan speed. It has nine cooking modes, including air fry and roast, and the body measures about 11.8 by 11.9 by 14.4 inches. It costs $50 to $100.

It wins because fan speed control is the feature that separates a good air fryer from a small convection oven: you can run a gentle fan for delicate foods and full speed for crisp finishes. The square basket makes better use of floor area than a round one. Against the OLIXIS it holds food in one zone, so you cook one thing at a time.

Buy it for a family of three to five who air fry several nights a week. The caveat is price, as it uses much of the $100 budget.
products.idealFor: Families who air fry several nights a week.
products.skipIf: You want two different foods at the same time.

products.name: OLIXIS Dual Air Fryers with 2 Baskets 9.5 Quarts Large Airfryer 10-in-1
products.verdict: Two 4.5 litre baskets with independent temperatures and a sync-finish mode.
products.description:
The OLIXIS has two separate baskets of 4.5 litres each, independent temperature control from 80 to 450F, and 10 one-touch presets. Match Cook copies settings across both baskets, and Sync Finish times two different foods to end together. A sensor sounds an alarm when it is time to shake, and the crisper plates are ceramic coated. The body is stainless steel at about 15.9 by 11.5 by 13.9 inches. It costs $50 to $100.

Second place reflects that a dual-basket fryer solves the biggest air fryer complaint, which is batch cooking. Each basket takes about a pound of fries, a whole chicken or a 6-inch pizza, according to the listing. It gives up a little on fan control compared with the Cosori and takes more counter space.

Choose it for family dinners with a main and a side. It is bulkier, and two baskets mean two items to wash.
products.idealFor: Mains and sides at the same time.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer Pro, 5 Qt, 4-in-1, Grey, AF141
products.verdict: A 1750W air fryer with a 5 quart basket that takes 4 lb of fries or 5 lb of wings.
products.description:
The AF141 is a 5-quart model with four functions, air fry, roast, reheat and dehydrate, a 1750W element and a 400F maximum. The nonstick basket and crisper plate fit up to 4 lb of fries or 5 lb of wings, and the design is meant to save counter space without losing capacity. It is about 11.3 by 10.4 by 14.8 inches and costs $50 to $100.

Third place comes from a lower ceiling: the maximum temperature is 400F, 50 degrees less than the Chefman and Cosori models, and there is no dual zone or window. The wattage is high for the class, which helps recovery after you open the basket.

Buy it if you want a proven, simple air fryer with a generous basket. The maker's fat-reduction figure comes from the brand's own comparison, so ignore it when choosing.
products.idealFor: Households wanting a straightforward, high-wattage 5 quart.

products.name: bella Fits-anywhere Slim 4qt Air Fryer, Non-Toxic Ceramic Coating, Oatmilk
products.verdict: A narrow 4 quart fryer with an EverGood ceramic coating and a basket that takes 3.3 lb.
products.description:
The bella is a slim 4-quart air fryer with an XL basket rated for 3.3 lb of food, 1300W of power, circular heat, and six presets: air fry, bake, roast, broil, reheat and dehydrate. Its EverGood ceramic nonstick coating is described as free of PFAS, PFOA, PTFE, lead and cadmium. It is about 8.2 by 11.1 by 14.6 inches and costs $30 to $50.

It ranks fourth because it is the best choice for small kitchens, and the cheapest of the ceramic models, but 1300W is the lowest wattage here, which means slower recovery and less crisp on large loads. The narrow shape also stacks food deeper.

Buy it for one or two people, a dorm or a small counter. A family of four will outgrow it quickly.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens and one or two people.
products.skipIf: You cook for a family of four or more.

products.name: Sweetcrispy Air Fryer 6 Quarts with Window, 12-in-1 Square Airfryer Oven for Family, 400F Rapid Air
products.verdict: A 6.34 quart square basket with a viewing window and 12 one-touch presets.
products.description:
The Sweetcrispy offers a 6.34 quart square basket that fits a whole chicken or four to six servings, a clear window so you can watch food without opening the basket, 12 presets, and a 400F maximum. The basket and accessories are nonstick and dishwasher safe. It is about 12.9 by 13.6 by 10.5 inches and costs $30 to $50.

Fifth place reflects a good size at a low price with a gap in detail: the listing gives no wattage, no fan specification and no named coating, and the temperature ceiling is 400F. The window is useful for browning checks.

Buy it if you want a family-size basket at a lower price and like to watch your food. Skip it if you want documented specs.
products.idealFor: Families who want a window and a big basket for less.
products.skipIf: You want documented power and coating.

products.name: CHEFMAN Multifunctional Digital Air Fryer+ Rotisserie, Dehydrator, Convection Oven, 17 Touch Screen Presets
products.verdict: A 10 litre oven-style air fryer with a rotisserie spit, three racks and 17 presets.
products.description:
This Chefman is an oven-style air fryer with 10 litres of capacity, 17 touch-screen presets, a rotisserie spit with a retrieval tool, three air flow racks and a drip tray. It can air fry, bake, dehydrate, rotisserie and roast, and has interior lights and a large window. It measures about 12 by 15 by 12 inches and costs $50 to $100.

It places sixth because the oven design needs more room and cleaning is harder than for a basket model, but it can cook a whole rotisserie chicken or several racks of food at once, which no basket here can.

Choose it for meal prep and roasting. For quick fries and wings, a basket model is easier.
products.skipIf: You want a fast basket-style fryer.

products.name: Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt TurboFry 4-in-1 with 450F Hi-Fry Option
products.verdict: An 8 quart fryer with a 450F Hi-Fry finish, a cETL approval and a one-year warranty.
products.description:
The TurboFry 8 qt has four presets for fries, chicken, meat and fish, a 450F Hi-Fry option, a nonstick basket and a flat frying tray that are top-rack dishwasher safe, and a cETL approval with a one-year warranty. The stainless exterior is square and about 13.5 by 10 by 12.75 inches. It costs $50 to $100.

Seventh place follows because an 8-quart basket this deep cooks less evenly than a wide one, and it has only four presets. The 450F option and the stated safety approval and warranty are real positives.

Buy it for a large family that wants a big basket and a clear warranty.
products.idealFor: Large families who want a big basket and warranty.
products.skipIf: You want a wide, shallow basket.

products.name: Chefman Air Fryer 4 QT Compact Airfryer with Hi-Fry Technology
products.verdict: A narrow 4 quart fryer with a halfway shake alarm and a 450F finish for the last two minutes.
products.description:
This compact Chefman has a 4-quart basket, a digital touch screen with four presets, a Hi-Fry setting that raises the heat to 450F for the last two minutes, and an audible alarm halfway through to remind you to shake the food. The basket and rack are dishwasher safe, and the unit turns itself off when cooking ends or the basket is removed. It is about 10 by 10.2 by 13.8 inches and costs $50 to $100.

Last place follows because it costs the same as larger models in this range while delivering the smallest cooking area. The shake alert and automatic shutoff are thoughtful.

Buy it for one or two people if you can find it cheaper. A bella at $30 to $50 gives more value.
pros: Auto shutoff when basket is removed
cons: Costs as much as bigger fryers
products.idealFor: Singles who want the shake reminder.

methodology.title: Basket shape and capacity
methodology.description: We favour wide, square baskets and honest capacity figures over the biggest quart number, since surface area drives crispness.

methodology.title: Fan and heat
methodology.description: Wattage, fan speed control and temperature range, up to 450F, decide how crisp and how even the food is.

methodology.title: Coating and cleaning
methodology.description: PFAS-free ceramic or nonstick coatings and dishwasher-safe baskets affect long-term use.

methodology.title: Extra features
methodology.description: Dual zones, windows, shake alerts and rotisserie accessories add value only if you will use them.

methodology.title: Value inside the cap
methodology.description: Many picks cost $50 to $100, so each must justify itself against $30 to $50 alternatives.

whatMatters.detail: A wide, shallow basket spreads food in a single layer, so hot air reaches every surface and fries crisp. A deep narrow basket piles food up and needs more shaking. Look at the dimensions and basket shape, and prefer a square design if you cook for a family.

Wattage drives how fast an air fryer heats, and fan speed drives how well the hot air moves. A 1750W unit recovers faster after the basket is opened than a 1300W one. Check the wattage in the listing, and note whether the fan speed is adjustable.
Most air fryers stop at 400F, and some reach 450F for extra crisp finishes. A low minimum, such as 80 or 90F, helps with dehydrating and proofing. Check both ends of the range.

Nonstick baskets can be PFAS-free ceramic or a traditional coating, and both scratch if you use metal tools. Ceramic is a selling point for many buyers, but it does not change how food cooks. Look for a named coating and dishwasher-safe baskets.

Two baskets let you cook a main and a side with synchronised finish. A window avoids opening the basket, and a shake alert reminds you to turn the food. These extras matter for convenience, not for how crisp the food is.

howToChoose.intro: Capacity should follow the number of people you cook for, but shape matters as much as quarts.

cards.label: Single basket
cards.text: Simpler, cheaper to run and easier to clean. The Cosori, Ninja and Sweetcrispy are examples, and a wide basket handles a family-size main.

cards.label: Dual basket
cards.text: Two independent baskets with sync modes, as on the OLIXIS. It suits dinners with a main and a side finishing together, at the cost of space and washing up.

howToChoose.note: Choose single unless you cook two items at once most nights.

rows: Ninja Air Fryer Pro 5 Qt AF141

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A narrow body, a handle that does not need clearance behind and a basket that fits the dishwasher. Compact does not need to mean tiny capacity.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The bella is only about 8.2 inches wide, the Chefman 4 qt is about 10 by 10.2 inches, and the Ninja AF141 is designed to save counter space with a 5 quart basket.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a larger dual-zone fryer with smart probes, an oven-style unit with steam, or a longer warranty. Models above $100 add those and sturdier build.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You air fry fries, wings and vegetables. The Sweetcrispy and bella cost $30 to $50, and the Cosori at $50 to $100 is the one upgrade worth making.

faq.q: Can I use foil or parchment in these air fryers?
faq.a: Perforated parchment liners and small pieces of foil work in most baskets if they are weighed down by food, and they must never cover the air holes. Check the manual for your model, and never preheat with loose paper.

faq.q: What is the most common air fryer mistake?
faq.a: Overfilling the basket. Food needs space for air to circulate, so cook in batches or use the Cosori's wide basket or the OLIXIS's two baskets.

faq.q: Is the Cosori worth more than the Sweetcrispy?
faq.a: Yes if you value fan speed control, a documented ceramic coating and a quieter motor. The Sweetcrispy is a decent family-size basket for $30 to $50, but its listing gives less detail.
A short preheat of a few minutes helps browning on most models, and the oven-style Chefman lists no preheat need. Follow the manual, since preheating differs by model.

faq.q: How do I clean the basket?
faq.a: Let it cool, then wash by hand or in the dishwasher if it is listed as dishwasher safe. Use a soft sponge on ceramic and nonstick surfaces, and wipe the heating element area with a damp cloth when cool.
They avoid PFAS and some owners prefer them, but they do not change how well the food cooks. Both ceramic and traditional coatings last longer with gentle cleaning and plastic or silicone tools.

finalTake: The Cosori TurboBlaze 6-quart is the best air fryer under $100 because of its fan speed control, 450F ceiling and PFAS-free ceramic basket, and it uses most of the budget. The OLIXIS dual-basket is the pick for two-food dinners, the Ninja AF141 is the straightforward 5-quart, and the bella is the slim choice. Skip the smallest Chefman unless you find it cheaper.
